domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need the lowest-cost App Service hosting that runs your app on shared infrastructure. Which tiers run on shared virtual machines?
explanation: The Free (F1) and Shared (D1) tiers run your app on VMs shared with other customers, while Basic and higher provide dedicated instances. Shared tiers also cannot scale out.
hint: Signal: shared infrastructure → Free and Shared tiers (F1/D1).

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to use deployment slots for staging and zero-downtime swaps. What is the lowest App Service plan tier that supports deployment slots?
explanation: Deployment slots are available only in the Standard, Premium, and Isolated tiers. Free, Shared, and Basic do not support slots.
hint: Signal: deployment slots → Standard tier or higher.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to increase the CPU and memory available to a single web app. What should you do?
explanation: Scaling up (vertical) moves the app to a larger plan size with more CPU and memory. Scaling out adds instances for horizontal capacity but does not change per-instance resources.
hint: Signal: CPU and memory → scale up (change tier/size).

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to scale individual apps in the same plan independently of one another. What is the lowest App Service plan tier that supports per-app scaling?
explanation: Per-app scaling is supported starting with the Standard tier (and higher). Free, Shared, and Basic plans do not support per-app scaling.
hint: Signal: lowest tier with per-app scaling → Standard

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: Several apps run in a single Standard plan. When you scale out the plan, what happens to the apps?
explanation: Apps in the same plan share the plan's instances, so scaling out adds instances that all apps use together. Per-app isolation requires separate plans or the Isolated tier.
hint: Signal: same plan → apps share instances and scale together.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: Your web app requires the full .NET Framework rather than .NET Core or .NET 5+. Which App Service operating system must you select?
explanation: The full .NET Framework runs only on Windows App Service. Linux supports .NET Core and .NET 5+ but not the legacy .NET Framework.
hint: Signal: full .NET Framework → Windows App Service.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a custom domain on your web app at the lowest possible cost. Which tier should you choose?
explanation: The Free tier does not support custom domains. Shared (D1) is the lowest-cost tier that allows a custom domain.
hint: Signal: custom domain + lowest cost → Shared (Free has no custom domains).

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need full network isolation in a dedicated, single-tenant environment for your web apps. Which tier should you use?
explanation: The Isolated tier runs in an App Service Environment, providing dedicated single-tenant hardware and full network isolation not available in shared or multitenant tiers.
hint: Signal: dedicated, single-tenant, network isolation → Isolated (ASE).

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need scheduled backup and restore for a web app. What is the lowest App Service tier that supports backup?
explanation: Backup and restore require the Standard tier or higher. Basic, Shared, and Free do not support App Service backups.
hint: Signal: backup and restore → Standard tier or higher.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You have an app in the Free tier and need to scale out to multiple instances. Solution: Add more instances to the Free plan. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: The Free and Shared tiers run on shared VMs and do not support scale-out. You must scale up to Basic or higher to add instances.
hint: Signal: Free tier + scale out → Free/Shared cannot scale out.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need zero-downtime deployment using a staging slot and swap. Solution: Use a Basic tier plan with a deployment slot. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: Deployment slots are not available in the Basic tier. They require Standard, Premium, or Isolated, so a Basic plan with a slot cannot meet the goal.
hint: Signal: deployment slot → not available below Standard.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to set a scale set to a fixed number of instances immediately, without any metric-based rules. Which scaling method should you use?
explanation: Manual scale sets an immediate, fixed instance count. Autoscale uses metric or schedule rules and is not an instant fixed count.
hint: Signal: fixed count, no rules → manual scale.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a scale set to add instances automatically when average CPU exceeds 70 percent. What should you configure?
explanation: A custom autoscale rule scales out when a metric such as CPU percentage crosses a threshold. Upgrade and scale-in policies do not drive metric-based scaling.
hint: Signal: CPU threshold → autoscale rule (scale-out condition).

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to control which instances are removed first when a scale set scales in. What should you configure?
explanation: The scale-in policy determines the removal order (Default, NewestVM, or OldestVM). Upgrade policy and autoscale rules do not control removal order.
hint: Signal: which instances removed first → scale-in policy.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You change the VM image referenced by a scale set's model and use a Manual upgrade policy. What happens to existing instances?
explanation: With a Manual upgrade policy, changing the model affects only new instances; existing instances keep the old image until you trigger an upgrade.
hint: Signal: Manual upgrade policy → existing instances keep old image until upgraded.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a scale set to add instances automatically when CPU is high and remove them when it is low. Solution: Configure a custom autoscale rule based on CPU percentage. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: A custom autoscale rule can scale out above and scale in below CPU thresholds, matching the requirement.
hint: Signal: scale on CPU metric → autoscale rule meets the goal.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You configure a rolling upgrade for a scale set and enable max surge. What does max surge provide during the upgrade?
explanation: Max surge creates temporary extra instances beyond the maximum count during a rolling upgrade so capacity and availability are maintained while batches are updated.
hint: Signal: max surge → temporary extra instances to preserve capacity.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to use the same custom image across several scale sets in multiple regions. Solution: Share the image through an Azure Compute Gallery. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: An Azure Compute Gallery (formerly Shared Image Gallery) shares custom images across regions and subscriptions so multiple scale sets can use them.
hint: Signal: share image across regions → Azure Compute Gallery.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to use the same custom image across several scale sets in multiple regions. What should you use to share the image?
explanation: An Azure Compute Gallery (formerly Shared Image Gallery) replicates and shares custom images across regions and subscriptions. Managed disks and snapshots are single-region objects.
hint: Signal: share image across regions → an image gallery.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a scale set upgrade that updates instances in batches while keeping the rest available. Which upgrade policy should you use?
explanation: The Rolling upgrade policy updates instances in batches (optionally with max surge) so some instances remain available. Manual requires you to trigger upgrades, and Automatic updates all at once.
hint: Signal: update in batches, stay available → Rolling upgrade policy.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a scale set whose instances can use different VM sizes. Which orchestration mode should you use?
explanation: Flexible orchestration allows instances with different VM sizes and other per-VM configuration. Uniform orchestration requires identical instances.
hint: Signal: different VM sizes → Flexible orchestration.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to upgrade a scale set to a new image while keeping instances available throughout. Solution: Use a rolling upgrade with max surge. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: A rolling upgrade updates batches incrementally, and max surge adds temporary instances so availability is preserved during the upgrade.
hint: Signal: stay available during upgrade → rolling upgrade with max surge.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need a low-cost firewall that filters only network (L3/L4) traffic with DNAT. Which Azure Firewall tier should you use?
explanation: Azure Firewall Basic filters only L3/L4 traffic (network and DNAT rules) and is the low-cost tier for SMBs. It has no application (L7) rules.
hint: Signal: L3/L4 only, low cost → Basic tier.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to allow outbound HTTPS to specific fully qualified domain names only. Which Azure Firewall rule type should you use?
explanation: Application rules filter by FQDN at Layer 7. Network rules filter by IP, port, and protocol and cannot match FQDNs.
hint: Signal: allow specific FQDNs → application (L7) rules.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: Which Azure Firewall tiers support threat intelligence filtering of known-malicious traffic?
explanation: Threat intelligence (alert or alert-and-deny) is available in Standard and Premium. Azure Firewall Basic does not support threat intelligence.
hint: Signal: threat intelligence → Standard and Premium (not Basic).

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to detect and block malicious traffic based on known attack signatures. Which Azure Firewall Premium feature should you enable?
explanation: IDPS (Intrusion Detection and Prevention System) detects and blocks attacks by matching signatures. Threat intelligence blocks known-bad domains/IPs but is not signature-based IDPS.
hint: Signal: detect/block by signatures → IDPS.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need IDPS protection against known attack signatures. Solution: Deploy Azure Firewall Standard. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: IDPS is available only in Azure Firewall Premium. Standard does not include IDPS, so the goal is not met.
hint: Signal: IDPS → Premium only, not Standard.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to inspect encrypted HTTPS traffic by decrypting it at the firewall. Which Azure Firewall tier supports TLS inspection?
explanation: TLS inspection (decrypting and re-encrypting traffic) is available only in Azure Firewall Premium, which also provides IDPS and URL filtering.
hint: Signal: TLS inspection (decrypt HTTPS) → Premium tier.

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to filter outbound traffic by fully qualified domain name across all ports and protocols. Solution: Deploy Azure Firewall Basic. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: Basic supports application-level (SNI-based) FQDN filtering for HTTPS/SQL only. Network-level FQDN filtering across all ports and protocols requires Standard or higher.
hint: Signal: all ports and protocols → network-level FQDN filtering (Standard+), not Basic

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to block outbound access to websites by category, such as social networking. What is the lowest Azure Firewall tier that supports web category filtering?
explanation: Web content filtering (web categories) is available in Standard and Premium, so Standard is the lowest tier that supports it. Basic does not.
hint: Signal: web category filtering → Standard or Premium (lowest = Standard)

domain: Implement and manage virtual networking
prompt: You need to decrypt and inspect encrypted HTTPS traffic. Solution: Deploy Azure Firewall Premium and enable TLS inspection. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: Azure Firewall Premium supports TLS inspection to decrypt, inspect, and re-encrypt HTTPS traffic, meeting the goal.
hint: Signal: decrypt HTTPS → Premium TLS inspection meets the goal.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to group VMs so that planned maintenance reboots only a subset at a time. Which construct should you use?
explanation: An update domain is a group of VMs that can be rebooted together during planned maintenance. Spreading VMs across update domains keeps others available.
hint: Signal: planned maintenance reboot grouping → update domains.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to protect VMs from a failure of a single rack of hardware. What should you use?
explanation: Fault domains within an availability set place VMs on different racks sharing separate power and network, protecting against a single-rack failure.
hint: Signal: single rack failure → fault domains in an availability set.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to apply OS updates to VMs in an availability set without downtime. What should you do?
options: Update all VMs at once together
Update one domain at a time
explanation: Updating one update domain at a time keeps the other domains serving traffic, avoiding total downtime during the rolling update.
hint: Signal: update without downtime → one update domain at a time.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You perform a rolling upgrade on a scale set. What is true about availability during the update?
explanation: A rolling upgrade updates instances in batches, so only the current batch is affected while the remaining instances stay available.
hint: Signal: rolling upgrade → only the current batch is affected.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You want the fewest VMs possible rebooted at once during planned maintenance. What is the default maximum number of update domains in an availability set?
explanation: An availability set can span up to 20 update domains by default, so VMs can be spread to minimize how many reboot together.
hint: Signal: maximum update domains → 20.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need protection against a failure of an entire datacenter within a region. What should you use?
explanation: Availability zones are physically separate datacenters in a region, protecting against datacenter-level failure. Fault and update domains protect within a single datacenter.
hint: Signal: whole datacenter failure → availability zones.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: Your VMs span three update domains. You update update domain 0 while it is isolated. How many update domains remain serving traffic?
explanation: If update domain 0 is being updated and isolated, the other two update domains continue to serve traffic.
hint: Signal: three update domains, one updating → two remain available.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need to keep VMs available while applying planned maintenance. Solution: Update one update domain at a time. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: Updating one update domain at a time keeps the remaining domains serving traffic, so availability is maintained during maintenance.
hint: Signal: keep available during maintenance → one update domain at a time.

domain: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources
prompt: You need a scale set upgrade that updates every instance at the same time. Solution: Use the Automatic upgrade policy. Does this meet the goal?
explanation: The Automatic upgrade policy updates all instances at once, matching the requirement to update every instance simultaneously.
hint: Signal: update every instance at once → Automatic upgrade policy.
